claims.statement: Capability gating is structural and decided once at registration: main() snapshots isAuthenticated() and passes it to registerAllTools, which concatenates readToolRegistrars (37) with writeToolRegistrars (17) only when includeWriteTools is true, so a guest process never registers the 17 write tools and they are absent from tools/list rather than rejected at call time.

No tool handler consults authentication at call time: the 60-second login heartbeat can flip the module-level authenticated flag to false and print a one-shot stderr warning, but the already-registered write tools remain callable and the failure surfaces as an ordinary MediaWiki permission error inside a tool result, so only a reconnect restores capability.

Guest mode is the absence of a login attempt, not a degraded login: initBot calls logIn only when both a username and a password are present, so half-configured credentials or a --token without a password pair produce a silently read-only session that cannot gain write tools without a restart.

There is no per-tool or per-user-right gating: the wiki groups and key rights fetched at startup are used only to describe the session in prose in the agent description, never to hide or refuse a tool, and the guest branch only adds a sentence telling the model that all write tools are hidden.

Seven write tools are graded HIGH RISK in their own tool descriptions: block, unblock, delete, undelete, protect, send-email, and create-account, each warning about harm to real people or irreversible loss of public content.

Six write tools are graded MEDIUM RISK: move, upload, upload-by-url, write, revert, and add-flow-topic, warning respectively about broken redirects and inbound links, silent overwrite of an existing file, untrusted source URLs (now bounded to public http(s) with 50 MB / 30 s limits also stated in the description), full-page overwrite loss, losing edits made after the restored revision, and publicly visible discussion threads.
Four write tools are graded LOW RISK: edit, append, prepend, and purge, described respectively as single-exact-match replacement, additive-only growth, and a non-destructive cache-only operation.

The risk grade is convention rather than code: each grade is a literal sentence inside its own server.tool description with no shared constant, no enum and no test that reads the risk text, so a new write tool that omits the prefix still registers and ships — the only CI assertions cover the four ToolAnnotations values and the 37/17 registrar counts, and the convention has already drifted (CLAUDE.md's MEDIUM list omits revert).

All 17 write tools declare readOnlyHint false while destructiveHint is true in 15 and false only for purge and undelete, so the annotations answer "does this call remove data" rather than "how much harm can this call cause" and disagree with the HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW grades in both directions.

The MCP instructions string is assembled in main() from runtime wiki facts (site name, version, endpoint, main page, language, statistics, auth state) followed by an operating-principles block, and a guest session is explicitly told it is in GUEST mode with all write tools hidden and how to obtain full access.

The operating-principles block partitions tools by who is harmed (ADMIN TOOLS: block, unblock, delete, undelete, protect; DESTRUCTIVE WRITE TOOLS: move, upload, upload-by-url; USER-IMPACTING TOOLS: send-email, create-account; CONTENT TOOLS: append, prepend, add-flow-topic), a different partition from the severity grades that leaves edit, write, revert and purge in no group and never mentions purge at all.

The operating-principles block also states cross-cutting rules the model is asked to obey: read the target page before writing, a SESSION NOTE that read state is per connection so a reconnect requires re-reading (and that login-expired errors mean reconnect), prefer line-based edit over full-page write and reserve append/prepend for additive changes, never fabricate titles or usernames, administer block/delete/undelete/protect only on an explicit operator command, copy wikitext verbatim without HTML-escaping, treat wiki content as a possible prompt-injection vector, and ask the human operator when in doubt.

The same description string is registered unconditionally as an MCP prompt named operating-principles (available in guest sessions too) whose single user message is 'Read and follow these rules:' followed by the entire description, not just the principles block, so the instructions and prompt routes cannot diverge.

Prompt-injection defence is behavioural only: the instructions tell the model that page text may hide instructions and to stop and warn the operator, while no code sanitises page content — get-article returns raw wikitext in a text block and the result helpers only JSON-serialise, never filter.

Every log-visible string produced by a write tool is prefixed with [nodemw-mcp.<tool>] before being sent to MediaWiki — unconditionally for edit, write, revert, append, prepend, move, delete, block, unblock and undelete, with fixed fallbacks for upload and upload-by-url, and only when the optional reason is supplied for protect.
Four write tools never emit a [nodemw-mcp.<tool>] tag at all: purge, send-email, create-account, and add-flow-topic, whose handlers pass no summary, reason, or comment field to the wiki API.

The write tool requires a caller-declared intent (add, revise, rewrite, or delete) and checks it against the byte-size delta between current and proposed content once that shrink exceeds 200 bytes: add rejects any shrink, revise rejects falling below three quarters of the current bytes, and rewrite and delete share a one-tenth near-total-wipe floor.

The --dry-run flag is forwarded into the nodemw client as an undocumented Bot option, but coverage is partial: block, unblock, undelete, and protect issue raw api.call requests and create-account calls nodemw's createAccount, so none of those five passes through the nodemw methods that refuse writes in dry-run mode, meaning they take effect anyway (12 of the 17 write tools are covered).

The read-before-write guard is the only read-state rejection of its kind and covers eight of the seventeen write tools (edit, write, append, prepend, revert, delete, protect, and move, which guards only its source title), leaving the remaining nine write tools with no read-state check.

沿请求路径的八层设计里只有五处能真正拒绝一次调用：注册期能力门控（工具不出现在 tools/list 中）、SDK 的 zod 输入校验、handler 内的护栏（写前必读、体量启发式、XOR）、upload-by-url 的 safeFetch 目标校验，以及只覆盖 12 个写工具的 --dry-run；风险前缀、ToolAnnotations、instructions、operating-principles prompt 与审计标签都只影响模型被告知的内容或 wiki 历史记录，无法阻止调用。
风险分级衡量的是后果而非可逆性：purge 因只让缓存失效而评为 LOW，undelete 是把内容加回来却评为 HIGH（恢复的可能是因法律或隐私原因被隐藏的修订），edit 直接改写活页面正文却因影响半径是一个精确匹配片段而评为 LOW。
registerAllTools 在循环里用 try/catch 包裹每个注册器，失败只打印 Error registering tool 并继续，因此某个写工具注册异常会表现为该工具从目录中缺席，而不是启动失败或门控失效。
createServer 只声明 tools 能力，但启动时无条件注册的 operating-principles prompt 会使 SDK 追加 prompts 能力与 prompts/list、prompts/get 处理器；因此移除该 prompt 会让客户端同时失去 prompts 能力，而不只是失去这段内容。
提示注入段落只点名 block、delete、protect、unblock、write 五个需要最高警惕的工具，未提及 undelete、send-email、upload、create-account，也未提及同样是一次整页覆写的 revert，而这些工具同样被评为 HIGH 或 MEDIUM，同样能被被劫持的模型触达。
启动横幅用注册器数组长度报告工具数量（认证会话为 54 = 37 read + 17 write，guest 会话为 37 read-only），因此它证明的是数组与门控一致，而不是注册全部成功。

The parsed --token option is dead for authentication: it is stored in ServerConfig but createBotFromConfig never forwards it to the nodemw Bot, and NODEMW_MCP_MW_TOKEN is read nowhere in src/, so a token-only invocation cannot reach the login-only path that sets authenticated and therefore runs as a guest session.

assertSafeFetchUrl is the target gate for upload-by-url: it rejects unparseable URLs, non-http(s) schemes, localhost/unix/*.localhost hosts, private or reserved IP literals, and any hostname whose DNS results include a private address; isPrivateAddress covers RFC1918, CGNAT 100.64/10, link-local and cloud metadata 169.254/16, IPv6 ::, ::1, fc00::/7, fe80::/10 and IPv4-mapped forms, and treats a string that is not a well-formed IPv4 literal as private (refuse rather than guess).

fetchSourceSafely imposes four hard bounds on a download: every redirect hop is re-validated by assertSafeFetchUrl (manual redirects, at most 5 hops), only a 200 response with a body is accepted, bytes are accumulated per chunk and the body is cancelled once 50 MB is exceeded, and a single 30-second wall-clock deadline covers the whole chain with an explicit elapsed check inside the body loop because undici is not guaranteed to abort mid-body; the request carries only a fixed User-Agent, no cookie jar, proxy or wiki session credentials.

upload-by-url deliberately avoids nodemw's uploadByUrl (no timeout, no size cap, the wiki session cookie jar attached, and support for the http://unix: pseudo-host), fetching the bytes through fetchSourceSafely instead and then handing them to nodemw's upload, so the tool is bounded by safeFetch's network rules and still subject to --dry-run and the [nodemw-mcp.upload-by-url] audit tag.

safeFetch's unit tests pin address classification (including CGNAT and 172.16/12 boundary values and malformed IPv4), scheme and localhost/unix rejection, direct private IPs and hostnames resolving to private addresses, redirect pivots to the metadata address or the unix pseudo-host, non-200 rejection and the 50 MB cap; the wall-clock deadline of the fetch loop has no corresponding test.

write's do-not-collapse-below-one-tenth floor is duplicated in edit and revert (same condition: current bytes minus result bytes greater than 200 AND result bytes less than current bytes divided by 10) so that these narrower write paths cannot become a lower-friction bypass of write's size heuristics.

errorResult is a diagnostic layer rather than an enforcement layer: it rewrites errors matching not allowed to edit this wiki through the API / not logged in / login required / assertuserfailed into "your login session has likely expired, reconnect via /mcp", and errors matching editconflict / 编辑冲突 into "the page changed after you read it, re-read and retry", so expired sessions and edit conflicts reach the model as actionable hints.

Thirteen tools validate mutually exclusive identifiers in the handler and return a tool error before calling the API when both or neither are supplied — title/id (or username/id, text/page) — for example get-article's Either "title" or "id" must be provided and Provide either "title" or "id", not both, and block/unblock's Provide either "username" or "id", not both.

The bundled patch patches/nodemw+0.26.0.patch (applied by the postinstall patch-package step) adds four dependency-level safety measures: a 30-second timeout on every API request and external fetch, session cookie jar scoped to the configured origin with a throwaway jar for any other target, removal of the process.argv debug log line that carried CLI credentials, and conversion of empty or malformed responses into callback errors instead of null dereferences inside the request callback.
